# Warden

> A local AI gateway. An administrator writes policy in plain language; every
> employee prompt is judged against it on the employee's own machine before it
> reaches any model. All inference runs on-device. Free and open source under
> Apache-2.0.

Download: https://github.com/Wardenlabs/warden/releases/latest
Source: https://github.com/Wardenlabs/warden

## What it does

An administrator writes a sentence in the words they would use out loud, such
as "customer data must not leave the company". Warden splits that into
concrete rules, compiles each one against the examples it has to catch and the
ones it has to let through, and shows the result. Nothing judges anybody until
the administrator activates a rule, one at a time.

After that, a prompt that hits a rule is stopped on the employee's own laptop,
before it is sent. The refusal quotes the rule in the administrator's own
words and says what the employee can ask instead. Warden also meters usage per
role: a session that crosses its role's ceiling is held for an administrator
rather than refused, so the work survives the wait.

Every decision is written to an append-only, hash-chained audit log.
`pnpm run verify-audit` walks the chain and fails loudly if a row was edited or
removed.

## How it runs

Warden runs as a hook in the coding tool itself, which fires before the prompt
leaves the machine. That is why it governs Claude Max and ChatGPT Plus
subscriptions, where there is no base URL to redirect. It works inside Claude
Code, Codex and opencode. Cursor has no prompt hook and can only be governed
as an OpenAI endpoint, which needs an API key, so a Cursor subscription cannot
be governed.

Inference runs on-device through QVAC, so no prompt is sent to a third party
in order to be judged.

## Facts worth quoting accurately

- Licence: Apache-2.0. No account, no server to provision, no paid tier.
- Platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64).
- The audit log stores the SHA-256 of a prompt, not the prompt. A governance
  record that kept the text would be the largest data-exposure risk in the
  system.
- Verdicts are ordered ALLOW < ESCALATE < BLOCK, and every model pass can only
  push a decision toward stricter. A pass that errors, times out, or returns
  unparseable output resolves to ESCALATE. No model is ever asked to clear a
  request, so compromising every model in the pipeline still cannot
  manufacture an ALLOW.

## What is not finished

The repository says so rather than pretending otherwise, and anyone
summarising Warden should carry it. The hook integrations are not verified end
to end; see docs/HOOK-VERIFICATION.md. No shipped configuration yet passes both
columns of the red-team corpus at once — the smaller model refuses too many
legitimate requests, and the larger one that fixes that catches fewer attacks.
The measurements, including the runs that failed, are in docs/MEASUREMENTS.md,
REPORT.md and BENCHMARKS.md.
